f. Some say Cadmus was the son of Agenor, others of Phoenix. Pherecydes in his fourth book says as follows (3 fg 21 J.): ‘Agenor, son of Poseidon, married Damno, daughter of Belus. Their children were Phoenix and Isaie, whom Aegyptus married, and Melia, whom Danaus married. Then Agenor married Argiope, daughter of the river Nile; their child was Cadmus.’

1191-92. The sun went down far away to the dark earth: he means the setting below the horizon; for he has said ‘dark’ because of the Erebus handed down by the ancients. He calls the Ethiopians those towards the setting, and ‘dark earth’ the invisible hemisphere around Erebus; such must be understood as the place below the horizon in Apollonius. He has called the sun ‘evening’, indicating the hour at which its setting follows. He has called the ‘uttermost peaks’ of the Ethiopians their farthest parts as lying beyond the inhabited world. But he has not correctly said that the sun sets beyond the peaks of the Ethiopians; for the horizon circle, not existing in nature, is marked by sight.
